The metrical-tree positional-encoding experiment, run as a REAL vs SHUFFLED control pair (both arms present: e3_metrical/real and e3_metrical/shuffled). The shuffled arm destroys metrical structure while preserving everything else, so the real-minus-shuffled delta is the whole measurement — read these two together or not at all. ⚠ WEAK: I could not find a doc naming who commissioned it or when; EXPERIMENTS.md's 'E3' is a DIFFERENT item (LatCH head re-validation), so do not resolve the label that way.

CONTINUITY 2026-08-17, Kim direct: "stage yet one more fp32 full-ft comparison at t512: lr 3e-5 and 1e-4 (I have a feeling Fusion goes fast, I want to see about a bit slower rates if it finds some smaller paths to new places), EMA, batch of 2, GAS 2... Datasets: suomisoundi, goa large, avp aug x8 ... #1 hyperball, #2 EDM2, #3 both." Six arms = 3 MODES x 2 LRs, testing whether bounding the fine-tune's DESTINATION (unlike warmup/EMA/AdaGC, which bound the path) prevents the drone/latent-scale runaway. hyperball = whole-tensor ‖W‖_F frozen at ‖W0‖_F optimizer-side on every spectral matrix; edm2 = per-output-channel direction normalised with a learnable per-channel gain on the output projection only (weaker, more expressive); both = hyperball on the bulk + gain control at the output. Both retrofit-safe (reproduce the pretrained function at step 0). ⚠ Hyperball (arXiv 2606.16899, Wen/Dang/Lyu/Ma/Liang) fixes norms to HYPERPARAMETER-DERIVED CONSTANTS, not to init — freezing at ‖W0‖_F is OUR choice, not the paper's.

purpose: CONTINUITY 2026-08-17, Kim direct: "stage yet one more fp32 full-ft comparison at t512: lr 3e-5 and 1e-4 (I have a feeling Fusion goes fast, I want to see about a bit slower rates if it finds some smaller paths to new places), EMA, batch of 2, GAS 2... Datasets: suomisoundi, goa large, avp aug x8 ... #1 hyperball, #2 EDM2, #3 both." Six arms = 3 MODES x 2 LRs, testing whether bounding the fine-tune's DESTINATION (unlike warmup/EMA/AdaGC, which bound the path) prevents the drone/latent-scale runaway. hyperball = whole-tensor ‖W‖_F frozen at ‖W0‖_F optimizer-side on every spectral matrix; edm2 = per-output-channel direction normalised with a learnable per-channel gain on the output projection only (weaker, more expressive); both = hyperball on the bulk + gain control at the output. Both retrofit-safe (reproduce the pretrained function at step 0). ⚠ Hyperball (arXiv 2606.16899, Wen/Dang/Lyu/Ma/Liang) fixes norms to HYPERPARAMETER-DERIVED CONSTANTS, not to init — freezing at ‖W0‖_F is OUR choice, not the paper's.

purpose: The R2(t)-gate mode A/B + seed pairs (CONTINUITY 2026-08-06, burn-day 2026-08-21). Identical to the subspace-loss grid EXCEPT the basis: melody_subspace15_selective_v3 instead of v2. Motivated by the melody machinery-audit — the v2 basis (top-15 melody VARIANCE) had ~ZERO melody-vs-codec-noise selectivity on held-out data (SNR 1.0x), so upweighting it boosted codec hiss as much as melody, the probable reason #59 came back weak. v3 (whitened CSP) is 5.1x melody-over-codec-noise held-out. K in {2,5,12}, matched to the v2 grid so arms compare directly. || The original SUBSPACE-WEIGHTED RF LOSS grid (CONTINUITY 2026-07-30, Kim direct). Counter to diffusion spectral bias (tau ~ 1/lambda, arXiv 2503.03206): melody is a measured 15-dim latent subspace holding only 9.3% of corpus variance, so plain RF gradient-starves it. Upweights the RF error's melody-subspace component by K (loss = mse + (K-1)*subspace_share; K=1 is byte-identical to off). K in {2,5,12}. Recipe = lreq_goa_lr1e4 EXACTLY, so the lr-equiv middle arm IS the K=1 baseline and no extra baseline burn was needed. ⚠ This grid used the v2 (melody-VARIANCE) basis later shown to have ~zero held-out selectivity — see subloss_tgate_modes for the v3 replacement. ⚠ AMBIGUOUS KEY: this run-directory name occurs under more than one campaign (lumi/sbatch/subloss_tgate_modes.sbatch, lumi/sbatch/subspace_loss_grid.sbatch); the variants above are the candidates and are usually the same experiment ported between containers.
